newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Light deferral to cost in long-run.
newsitem.headline: China Light deferral to cost in long-run.

text.p: China Light & Power Co Ltd, which agreed to delay fully bringing onstream its Black Point power station, said on Monday that postponement to units seven and eight will cost consumers in the longer-term.

"In the longer term there will be additional costs, because those two units, when we do come to install them, they will cost more, so in the longer-term there will be a cost," general manager Peter Littlewood told government radio.
Littlewood, however, said the move would be beneficial to electricity users in the shorter term.
"In the shorter term, there is a benefit to consumers. The reason for that is that...by deferring them, we will be spending later," he said.
The company has agreed to defer the two units for up to five years if the situation requires but the government said in a statement it would review the situation in 1999.
The power supplier has also agreed to decommission shortly 442 megawatts of existing gas turbine capacity and to put the gas turbines into preservation.
The decommissioning of gas turbines will immediately hold down the reserve margin by 10 percent.
China Light has warned in the past that the deferral of the two units could cost the company between HK$200 million and HK$1.5 billion in additional costs.
The utility came under immense pressure to halt or defer the commissioning of some units of its eight-unit Black Point Power Station due to a slowdown in growth in electricity demand.
